text:
ConocoPhillips rose 1.6% today, building on a three-day rally that's pushed the stock up $5.60 since November 9th. The timing aligns with a shift in oil-market sentiment: crude prices have steadied in the $89–92 range after briefly dipping below $90 on hopes for an Iran peace deal, but Trump's recent comments suggesting the Iran conflict will end "fairly soon" appear to have eased some of the worst-case geopolitical risk premium that had weighed on energy stocks earlier in the week.

The broader context here is that energy stocks had sold off sharply through early November amid recession fears and a Democratic sweep in midterm elections that signaled headwinds for oil producers. ConocoPhillips is still down 6.7% over two weeks, so today's gain is a partial recovery—not a new bullish story, but a relief bounce as near-term geopolitical uncertainty recedes and oil prices find a floor.
